name: Luna 5
outcome_detail: A guidance gyroscope fault and a ground control error meant the braking engine never fired and the probe hit the Moon at full speed.
lesson: Failure was guidance and operations, not the site; the impact point itself is still disputed between sources.

name: Luna 7
outcome_detail: An optical sensor set at the wrong angle lost sight of Earth before retrofire, attitude control was lost, the engine was inhibited and the probe crashed in Oceanus Procellarum.
lesson: Attitude reference depended on keeping Earth in the sensor's view; the failure was not caused by the terrain.

name: Luna 8
outcome_detail: A bracket apparently pierced a landing airbag, the escaping gas spun the craft, the retro burn lasted only nine seconds and it crashed in Oceanus Procellarum.
lesson: Failure was mechanical (airbag puncture), unrelated to the landing site.

name: Luna 9
outcome_detail: First soft landing on the Moon; the airbag-protected capsule returned the first panoramas from the surface in Oceanus Procellarum.
lesson: Showed the mare surface can bear a lander; its exact position is still unconfirmed in orbital imagery 60 years later, so historical coordinates can be off by 10 km or more.

name: Surveyor 1
outcome_detail: First US soft landing, in Oceanus Procellarum near Flamsteed P; engines cut off about 3.4 m up and it dropped the rest of the way.
lesson: Flat mare was a forgiving first site, and the lander paused through the lunar night and still returned engineering data for months afterwards.

name: Surveyor 2
outcome_detail: One of three vernier engines failed to ignite at the midcourse correction, the craft tumbled, contact was lost on 22 September and it hit the Moon near Copernicus.
lesson: Failure was propulsion during cruise, unrelated to the intended Sinus Medii site; the crash site has never been located.

name: Luna 13
outcome_detail: Second Soviet soft landing, in Oceanus Procellarum, returning panoramas and soil mechanics measurements.
lesson: Confirmed mare regolith strength for later landers; like Luna 9 its position rests on 1960s tracking rather than orbital imagery.

name: Surveyor 3
outcome_detail: A radar anomaly kept the vernier engines firing so it lifted off and touched down again twice before settling inside a small crater in Oceanus Procellarum.
lesson: Landing radar confused near the surface caused the bounces, and the craft came to rest on the inner wall of a crater rather than on level ground.

name: Surveyor 4
outcome_detail: Radio contact was lost during terminal descent about 2.5 minutes before touchdown in Sinus Medii, possibly because the solid retrorocket exploded.
lesson: Failure was probably propulsion, not the site; the coordinates are only the predicted landing point and no wreckage has been located.

name: Surveyor 5
outcome_detail: Landed in Mare Tranquillitatis despite a helium leak that forced a shortened vernier engine sequence.
lesson: Survived its first lunar night and resumed transmitting on later lunar days, showing a solar-powered lander can sometimes wake after the two-week night.

name: Surveyor 6
outcome_detail: Landed in Sinus Medii and a week later fired its engines to hop about 2.5 m, the first liftoff from the lunar surface.
lesson: A flat central-nearside site with direct Earth visibility; it returned no useful data after its first lunar night.

name: Surveyor 7
outcome_detail: Landed on the outer rim of Tycho crater in the southern highlands and completed its science objectives.
lesson: Proved a landing on rough highland ejecta was possible, but the battery was damaged during the first lunar night and contact became sporadic.

name: Apollo 11
outcome_detail: First crewed landing, in Mare Tranquillitatis; Armstrong took semi-manual control to fly past a boulder field beside West crater.
lesson: Even a smooth mare ellipse contained a boulder-strewn crater at the computer's aim point, so hazard avoidance in the final seconds mattered.

name: Luna 15
outcome_detail: Sample-return attempt lost contact four minutes into descent and crashed in the Mare Crisium region, probably into the side of a mountain.
lesson: Descent over poorly known relief: the craft likely hit high ground that its trajectory planning had not accounted for.

name: Apollo 12
outcome_detail: Crewed pinpoint landing in Oceanus Procellarum within walking distance of Surveyor 3, which the crew visited.
lesson: Demonstrated precision landing next to a known surface target, on the rim of the crater holding Surveyor 3.

name: Luna 16
outcome_detail: First robotic sample return; landed in Mare Fecunditatis and lifted off after about 26 hours.
lesson: First landing made in lunar night (the Sun had set about 60 hours earlier), showing a radar-guided descent does not need sunlight.

name: Luna 17 / Lunokhod 1
outcome_detail: Landed in Mare Imbrium and deployed Lunokhod 1, the first rover, which worked for eleven lunar days.
lesson: Lunokhod survived repeated lunar nights by closing its solar-panel lid and using a polonium-210 heater.

name: Apollo 14
outcome_detail: Crewed landing at Fra Mauro after the landing radar failed to lock on until the crew cycled its breaker.
lesson: Undulating highland terrain made surface navigation hard: landmarks looked different from the maps and the crew stopped about 20 m short of Cone crater's rim without seeing it.

name: Apollo 15
outcome_detail: Crewed landing at Hadley-Apennine; the LM came down on the rim of a small crater the commander could not see.
lesson: An unseen small crater left the lander tilted about 7 degrees back and 9 degrees left, a reminder that metre-scale relief decides the final attitude.

name: Luna 18
outcome_detail: Sample-return attempt lost contact at the moment of landing in rugged highland terrain near Mare Fecunditatis.
lesson: The Soviets attributed the loss to landing in complex mountainous conditions; Luna 20 later succeeded about 1.8 km away.

name: Luna 20
outcome_detail: Sample return from the Apollonius highlands, landing about 1.8 km from where Luna 18 was lost.
lesson: A mountainous site can work and can fail within 2 km of each other: local slope at the touchdown point, not the region, decided the result.

name: Apollo 16
outcome_detail: Crewed landing in the Descartes highlands, the only Apollo landing in the central lunar highlands.
lesson: Crewed highland landing succeeded on cratered, blocky terrain with a pilot choosing the final spot.

name: Apollo 17
outcome_detail: Last crewed landing, on the floor of the Taurus-Littrow valley.
lesson: Landing on a valley floor between massifs required a precise approach, done with a crew and good lighting.

name: Luna 21 / Lunokhod 2
outcome_detail: Landed in Le Monnier crater and deployed Lunokhod 2, which drove about 37 km.
lesson: A flat lava-flooded crater floor at a mare-highland boundary gave a safe landing next to varied terrain.

name: Luna 23
outcome_detail: Landed in Mare Crisium but tipped onto its side, damaging the drill; no sample was returned and it transmitted for three days.
lesson: LRO images show it lying on its side, probably from excess vertical or horizontal velocity at touchdown: a tall lander falls over easily even on a mare.

name: Luna 24
outcome_detail: Last Soviet lunar landing; returned a drill core from Mare Crisium, a few kilometres from Luna 23.
lesson: Repeating the Luna 23 site succeeded, so that loss came from touchdown dynamics rather than an unsuitable region.

name: Chang'e 3 / Yutu
outcome_detail: First soft landing since 1976, in northern Mare Imbrium, deploying the Yutu rover.
lesson: Hovered at 100 m and translated sideways to avoid obstacles, and its radioisotope heater has kept the lander alive through many lunar nights.

name: Chang'e 4 / Yutu-2
outcome_detail: First soft landing on the lunar far side, in Von Karman crater, deploying the Yutu-2 rover.
lesson: The far side never sees Earth, so every command and all data went through the Queqiao relay satellite near Earth-Moon L2; radioisotope heaters carried it through the nights.

name: Beresheet
outcome_detail: An inertial measurement unit fault and the resulting computer resets shut down the main engine during braking and the lander hit Mare Serenitatis at over 500 km/h.
lesson: Failure was avionics and software, unrelated to the site.

name: Chandrayaan-2 Vikram
outcome_detail: A software fault during the braking phase left the lander unable to correct excess thrust and it crashed about 600 m from its target near 70.9 S.
lesson: Failure was guidance software, made worse by a rigid requirement to reach one small site; not caused by the terrain.

name: Chang'e 5
outcome_detail: Sample-return lander set down near Mons Rumker in Oceanus Procellarum and the ascender left about two days later.
lesson: With no radioisotope heater the lander finished its work inside one lunar day and died in the following night.

name: Hakuto-R Mission 1
outcome_detail: Software rejected the radar altimeter as faulty, the lander hovered about 5 km up until propellant ran out and fell into Atlas crater.
lesson: Software plus terrain: the altitude estimate went wrong while descending toward a crater, so the relief along the approach path has to be in the simulations, not just the landing spot.

name: Luna 25
outcome_detail: A pre-landing orbit-lowering burn ran 127 seconds instead of 84 and the craft struck the inner rim of Pontecoulant G crater, about 400 km short of its site near Boguslawsky.
lesson: Failure was propulsion control in orbit, unrelated to the intended south polar site.

name: Chandrayaan-3
outcome_detail: First soft landing near the lunar south pole; the Vikram lander and Pragyan rover worked for about 12 days.
lesson: Neither lander nor rover was built for the cold of lunar night and neither woke after sunset, so the mission was one lunar day long.

name: Peregrine Mission One
outcome_detail: A propellant leak after launch on 8 January 2024 ruled out a landing; the craft never descended to the Moon and re-entered Earth's atmosphere on 18 January 2024.
lesson: Failure was propulsion (suspected stuck valve and oxidizer tank rupture), unrelated to the intended Gruithuisen Domes site.

name: SLIM
outcome_detail: Precision landing within 100 m of its target near Shioli crater, but it lost an engine nozzle in descent and came to rest tilted about 90 degrees with its solar panels facing west.
lesson: Attitude decides power: with panels facing away from the morning Sun it had to wait for afternoon light, yet it then survived three lunar nights it was not designed for.

name: IM-1 Odysseus
outcome_detail: With its laser rangefinders unusable it landed faster than planned on a slope of about 12 degrees near Malapert A, broke a leg and came to rest tilted about 30 degrees.
lesson: A slope beyond the design limit plus missing altimetry tipped a tall lander; tilted antennas cut data rates and it lost power as lunar night began a week later.

name: Chang'e 6
outcome_detail: First sample return from the far side, landing in Apollo basin and lifting off about 49 hours later.
lesson: A far-side site has no direct line to Earth, so descent and surface work relied on the Queqiao-2 relay satellite.

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
outcome_detail: Fully successful commercial landing in Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille, operating for about 14 days.
lesson: Flat mare at mid latitude gave a full lunar day of sunlight and Earth contact; the solar-powered lander died about five hours after sunset.

name: IM-2 Athena
outcome_detail: Altimeter trouble during descent to Mons Mouton led to a hard touchdown; the lander skidded and ended on its side inside a 20 m shadowed crater, and the mission ended within 13 hours.
lesson: Near the pole a small crater is enough to put a lander in permanent shade and cold (-173 C); on its side in shadow it could not recharge.

name: Hakuto-R Mission 2 Resilience
outcome_detail: A laser rangefinder anomaly gave late altitude data, the lander could not slow in time and hit Mare Frigoris; contact was lost about 90 seconds before planned touchdown.
lesson: Failure was the altitude sensor, not the flat Mare Frigoris site.
